assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of GLP-1 as an incretin and its translation into GLP-1 receptor agonists has transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with additional cardiovascular and renal benefit signals. Mechanistic clarity, large clinical effect and enormous patient impact make this a leading candidate, and the CNS appetite-circuit angle also touches neuroscience.
assessment.attribution: Holst characterised native GLP-1 physiology, Mojsov contributed peptide chemistry and the active truncated form, and Drucker defined receptor biology and gut/pancreatic actions. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen (industry drug development) is a credible fourth name, so a three-person cap forces a difficult choice. Credit for the active GLP-1(7-36) form is historically contested and I have not independently verified details.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy is confirmed by many independent large outcome trials over more than a decade, and the field is mature and stable, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Precedence dispute over who established the active GLP-1 form
Whether drug-development credit (Knudsen) should displace a physiology laureate within a three-person limit
Long-term safety of chronic use is still accumulating

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living therapeutics. The concept is original and clinically validated, with lasting impact on cancer immunology.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led the translation of costimulated CAR designs (CD28 and 4-1BB) into clinical efficacy; Steven Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified lymphocyte trials. Original CAR conceptualisation (Eshhar and others) is not on the supplied list, which complicates a fair configuration. Choice between Rosenberg and Sadelain is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation across centres; long-term follow-up now spans more than a decade of cures in leukemia. Solid-tumour efficacy remains limited.
uncertainties: Credit for the original CAR concept lies outside the credited names
Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy role versus Sadelain's engineering role
Toxicity and limited activity in solid tumours

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) turned spinal muscular atrophy, previously a fatal infant disease, into a treatable condition. It is a clean example of mechanism-to-therapy translation and the first widely validated splice-modulating antisense drug.
assessment.attribution: Krainer elucidated the SMN2 splicing mechanism and identified the ISS-N1 target region, and Bennett led the antisense chemistry and development; the pairing is compact and coherent. Other contributors to SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) and ISS-N1 target work are not credited on this entry.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy has been confirmed in trials and real-world use for years, and the approach has spawned other RNA therapies. Timing is reasonable, though this may be seen as somewhat early relative to broader antisense validation.
uncertainties: Contributions of SMN gene discovery are outside the credited names
Possible need to recognise the antisense platform more broadly
Industry versus academic balance

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided a general method for cell-type-specific control of neural activity with light and transformed circuit neuroscience, with growing clinical translation (for example in vision restoration). It is original, widely adopted and central to modern experimental neuroscience.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth, Miesenboeck and others) are separate contributions, six credited names exceed the three-person limit, and any trio is contestable. I propose Deisseroth for neuronal application plus Nagel and Hegemann for the molecular discovery.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and reproduced across thousands of laboratories; the tool is mature. Clinical impact is still limited, so recognition rests mainly on research-tool impact.
uncertainties: Severe attribution crowding, with Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck omitted
Whether a methodological tool fits the physiology or medicine remit as strongly as a therapy
Clinical translation is still early

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identifying tau and alpha-synuclein as the principal components of neurofibrillary tangles, Pick bodies and Lewy bodies defined the molecular pathology of Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and related diseases and underlies fluid and PET biomarkers and seed-amplification assays. As a neurologist I regard the impact on diagnosis and staging as substantial.
assessment.attribution: Spillantini and Goedert did the decisive biochemical and immunohistochemical work for alpha-synuclein in Lewy bodies and tau filaments; the two-person configuration is clean. Others (for example Lee, Trojanowski, Braak) contributed to related findings and are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Strongly replicated and extended by cryo-EM filament structures and biomarker assays. Therapeutic payoff remains limited, which may make recognition less urgent than for validated treatments.
uncertainties: Overlap with contributions of others in the field, such as Lee and Trojanowski
Lack of an established disease-modifying therapy
Whether the discovery is judged complete or an ongoing programme

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of orexin/hypocretin and its loss in narcolepsy type 1 uncovered a specific neuropeptide system governing wakefulness, and it has led to orexin receptor antagonists for insomnia and agonists now in development. The finding is original, clear and mechanistically coherent.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa identified orexins and receptors; de Lecea and Kilduff independently identified hypocretins; Mignot positionally cloned the canine narcolepsy gene (HCRTR2). Independent simultaneous discovery makes allocation hard, and I picked Mignot to recognise the disease link, though de Lecea is equally arguable.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed through genetics, human pathology and approved antagonist drugs; mature and stable. Agonist therapy for narcolepsy is still emerging.
uncertainties: Near-simultaneous independent discovery of hypocretin and orexin
Choice between Mignot and de Lecea or Kilduff
Agonist therapeutic impact not yet established

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL kinase inhibition with imatinib created the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy and converted chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal to a manageable disease. Clarity and impact are exceptional, though the field has been widely recognised already.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the compound discovery programme, Druker drove clinical development and demonstrated efficacy, and Sawyers showed mechanisms of resistance and enabled second-generation inhibitors. Credit for the compound's chemistry (for example Zimmermann) and for the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL itself (Rowley, Nowell, Hungerford, Groffen and others) lies outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Decades of follow-up confirm durable survival and the model is stable; the long gap since approval means recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Upstream discovery of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion is not credited
Compound chemistry contributions are outside the list
Industry versus academic credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating that TNF is a central driver of rheumatoid arthritis and that its blockade is therapeutic launched the biologic era in autoimmune disease and benefited millions of patients with RA, Crohn's disease, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. The concept, from cytokine cascade to clinical proof, is clear and durable.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the mechanistic work and the first clinical trials of anti-TNF in RA; the pair is natural. Contributions to antibody engineering, to TNF's identification (Old, Cerami, Beutler) and to the infliximab development at industry are not credited and might be seen as part of a broader story.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed over decades by multiple agents and indications, with a mature record. Timing is long overdue, and biosimilar uptake shows broad clinical acceptance.
uncertainties: Upstream TNF discovery and antibody engineering credit lie outside the list
Whether the committee views this as clinical translation of known biology
Competing claims with other cytokine-blockade programmes
